newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE PESO WEIGHED DOWN BY REGIONAL MALAISE.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE PESO WEIGHED DOWN BY REGIONAL MALAISE.

text.p: The Philippine peso continued to be weighed down on Thursday by the malaise in the region's currencies, traders said.

It ended at 29.49 to the dollar, down from the previous close of 29.05 but up from the intraday low of 29.62. Trading was more active, with volume more than double at $150.8 million from $62.55 million.
"There is still uncertainty at this time. The market will favour the dollar as long as Southeast Asian currencies remain under pressure," a foreign bank trader said.
Traders said the central bank kept its hands off the market, which led to the further fall of the peso.
"It kept its offer rate for the dollar 10 centavos above the best offer. I think the central bank wants the market to find its own level," another trader said.
"We will test 30," the first trader said, saying there were large corporate requirements for dollars.
He said oil firms had started to scout around for $200 million to pay for their imported crude.
Other traders believed otherwise. "The market is up for a correction. This is not fundamentally driven," one dealer said.
